25th Anniversary (smaller font)
Slide 1 — 2001: It started with an email. Andrew Ross Sorkin, a 24-year-old M&A reporter at The New York Times, begins sending an informal daily newsletter.
Slide 2 — 2006: DealBook goes digital. The newsletter becomes a full site on NYTimes.com.
Slide 3 — 2011: DealBook takes the stage. The first DealBook Summit brings together leaders from business, politics, finance, technology, media and culture.
Slide 4 — 2026: Twenty-five years in, the Summit returns November 18 with the same mission, and the biggest stage yet.

column11:
Title SLIDE - Does It Help to Be Feared?
Underneath - Three CEOs, One Question.
Image would be a wider shot of the task force table. So we can see that the discussion is a round table-esque talk, and not a one on one interview. 

Slide 2 — Emma Walmsley, CEO, GlaxoSmithKline: “Fear...I never have that as an aspiration as a CEO because you want people to be able to bring you bad news — if they’re scared of doing that, you’re gonna have a real problem in terms of transparency and pace of decision-making.” (text overlays an image of Emma)

Slide 3 — Alex Chriss, CEO, PayPal: “Fear is very effective, but it has a ceiling. The way I try to lead is with head and heart — with inspiration and compassion. When you can mobilize thousands of people around an inspiration, the ceiling of what you can accomplish together is so much higher.” (text overlays an image of Alex)

Slide 4 — Bob Jordan, President & CEO, Southwest Airlines: “Fear is not sustainable. The only way you create trust is create vulnerability in the room — and it's only going to happen if I go first... Fear sustains for a while. Love sustains for a long time.” (text overlays an image of Bob)
